title: Database Connection Pooling
description: Manage a connection pool, execute parallel queries, monitor pool statistics, and test max connection limits.

steps.title: Pool health check
steps.description: Initialize a connection pool (size 5) on startup and expose GET /health that returns pool statistics including total, active, idle, and waiting connection counts.
hints: For JS/TS, use better-sqlite3 which is synchronous (single connection) - simulate pool stats
For Python, use sqlite3 with a simple connection pool wrapper
For Go, use database/sql which has built-in pooling via SetMaxOpenConns

steps.title: Parallel queries
steps.description: Execute 5 parallel queries against the pool. All should return 200. Use concurrent requests to test the pool can handle multiple simultaneous operations.
hints: Insert seed data first then query in parallel
Use Promise.all (JS) or goroutines (Go) for parallel execution

steps.title: Pool statistics endpoint
steps.description: Implement GET /stats that returns detailed pool statistics including active connections, idle connections, total requests, and wait time.
hints: Use db.Stats() in Go, manual counters for others

steps.title: Max connections test
steps.description: Set a max pool size of 3. Execute 10 rapid concurrent requests — only 3 should be active at once, others should wait. Report pool behavior in GET /health/stats.
hints: Simulate slow queries to observe queuing
